clue.text: Go without a piece of underwear in burlesque

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for go sits round the rest

parts.note: to have a go is to try
taken as written
a vest is an undershirt, a piece of underwear

explanation.surface: Someone performs in a comic stage show minus some undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the attempt wraps around the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a grotesque mocking imitation, which is what a travesty is too.

clue.text: Pronounced seam of mineral becomes worthless

indicators.note: pronounced says the word for the seam is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a vein is a seam of ore or mineral in rock

explanation.surface: A conspicuous mineral seam turns out to have no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective meaning obvious; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in vain is futile, of no worth or effect.

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
to lam is to beat or strike hard

explanation.surface: A conspiracy to down tools brings disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' wants to be a scheme; it is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, after the old London asylum, is uproar and utter confusion.

indicators.note: something done stupidly is done in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bulb planted foolishly turns out to be a thorny plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubble, short regrowth of beard, is bristly and rough to the touch, that which feels prickly.

clue.text: Rod holds paintings up for poet

indicators.note: holds says one word contains another

parts.note: a perch is an old measure of length, also called a rod

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: A stick supports pictures for a versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only makes sense in a down clue, where the paintings read upwards; 'holds' puts them inside the rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrarch was the fourteenth-century Italian poet famed for his sonnets to Laura.

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
tracing, as in tracking down, means hunting for

explanation.surface: Chasing serpents as a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Boat racing, as in rowing or sailing contests, is a competitive sport on water.

clue.text: Mogul is strangely coy when wearing the latest fashion

indicators.note: one wears clothes round oneself, so the fashion word is placed around the rest

parts.note: ton is an old word for the prevailing fashion

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of coy come out oddly ordered

explanation.surface: A powerful magnate is oddly bashful when dressed in modish clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' scrambles coy and 'when wearing' dresses it in the fashion word; ton for fashion is an old society usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful business magnate, which is the meaning of tycoon.

parts.note: taken as written
to style someone is to name or call them
NT is the New Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: Decorate or design a set of sacred texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' looks like fashion; it is the verb meaning to call.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament something is to decorate or embellish it, the verb sense.

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
spare means lean or thin, so bony

explanation.surface: A carrier of extra timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard dark wood from tropical trees.

clue.text: Russian leader starts to ignore very able negotiator

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A Russian head of state begins by snubbing a skilled diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was a Russian tsar, an example of a Russian leader.

clue.text: Freedom for Queen to tuck into drink

indicators.note: tucking something into a thing puts it inside, so the royal letters go within the drink

parts.note: a libation is a drink, especially one poured as an offering
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch gains liberty to get stuck into a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating or drinking heartily; here it means the royal cipher goes inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberation is the act of setting free, giving freedom.

clue.text: A quiet drive to religious retreat

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the call for quiet
to ram is to drive or force in

explanation.surface: A peaceful journey to a place of spiritual withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests a car trip; it is the verb, to ram.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or community for religious retreat.

clue.text: Showman to call Mark over bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the earlier pieces above the later

parts.note: to ring is to telephone, to call
M is short for mark, the old German currency
a bloomer here is a flower, the aster

explanation.surface: An entertainer phones Mark about a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder; it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringmaster directs a circus performance, a showman in charge of the ring.

clue.text: Learning about bad weather in France

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: Studying the poor climate across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place found in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorraine is a region of north-eastern France, so a place found within France.

indicators.note: terrible says the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: The CIA denies using an awful toxin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanide is a famously deadly chemical poison.

indicators.note: violated says the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A perfect ending broke the cut-off date.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the latest time by which something must be done, a limit in time.

parts.note: SH, s/h, is short for second-hand, or used
a river is a banker, something that has banks

explanation.surface: A father confessor was a second-hand financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' wants a financier; in crosswords it is a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrive is to hear confession and absolve, so a shriver is a confessor.

clue.text: Note on an Anglican church shows style

parts.note: E is a musical note
the on side is the leg side in cricket
taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A memo about an Anglican congregation displays flair.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side. 'Anglican' is part of the church: CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is graceful refinement, a synonym for style.

parts.note: re means about or concerning, touching on
Samuel Morse invented the telegraph code named after him

explanation.surface: Regret is a moving quality in a creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like moving; it means concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for wrongdoing, which is penitence.

clue.text: Bill gets a million marketing water

parts.note: an ad, a poster or bill, is an advertisement
taken as written
a sale is selling, marketing

explanation.surface: Bill earns a fortune selling drinking water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is an advertising bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for plain water, the only drink of the first man.

parts.note: to do a thing is to produce or make it

indicators.note: rude means rough or unrefined, so the letters of sign are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Making an offensive gesture for events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude sign' suggests an obscene gesture; 'rude' rearranges SIGN into INGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doings are things done or happening, activities or events.

clue.text: One erecting scaffold to start going topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the first letter, the top of the word

parts.note: to trigger something is to start it off

explanation.surface: A builder of staging begins to work without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests nudity; it drops the opening T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigger is a worker who puts up scaffolding or rigging.

indicators.note: loses says a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a runaway is a fugitive
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An escapee drops a bag at the terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a thing found at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip at an airport where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Let Winston run amok in Hollywood

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Allow Churchill to go berserk in the film capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood, alluding to its showy glamour.

definitions.meaning: made of ..., the soft pine or fir timber, as in a ... table
to ... with something is to handle it

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is fir or pine wood, and to deal with is to handle or manage.

parts.note: aft means behind, toward the stern

explanation.surface: Arriving a day late? How ridiculous!
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is a British informal word for foolish or silly.

indicators.note: after puts the word for rest behind the letter for good

parts.note: to lean on something is to rest on it

explanation.surface: Take a break once the crop has done well.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover grain after reaping, so a kind of harvesting.

parts.note: a stole is a scarf worn round the shoulders
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A villainous mobster took a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like the past of steal; it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of Al Capone, the notorious Chicago gangster.
